evidence.positive: Against the shipped 100ab1bd9 build at localhost:61153, launched a demo-demo case end to end as loopuser: POST /api/generate-app-launch-key then POST /api/app-launch {patientId: patient-1, caseId: CL83301} returned 200 with the full ApplicationLaunchContext (mrn patient-1, Test Tester, 83 kg), so the app-launch path the deleted branch sat in front of completes normally. GET /actuator/metrics/orci.case.launch went from 404 (meter not yet registered) to 200 with measurements COUNT 1.0 and availableTags [{"tag":"mode","values":["INTERACTIVE"]}] - the counter still records the launch and now carries only the mode tag. GET /actuator/env contains no case-launcher key at all, /actuator/beans contains no caselauncher bean, and /app/libs in the container holds no case-launcher artifact.
evidence.negative: Reinstated the deleted flag on the running app: wrote case-launcher.enabled=true to /application.properties inside the container (working dir is /, so Spring binds it via optional:file:./) and restarted. /actuator/env then listed it under "Config resource 'file [application.properties]' via location 'optional:file:./'", confirming the property was live. POST /api/app-launch {patientId: patient-2, caseId: CL83302} still returned 200 with the full launch context, and orci.case.launch again reported availableTags [{mode: INTERACTIVE}] with no case_launcher tag. The flag is inert - setting it no longer selects any branch, and no case_launcher tag reappears.
evidence.red_check: Two flips, both reverted and re-verified. (1) Class swap: compiled the parent-commit AppLaunchController (7e1dc76d7^, with @Slf4j expanded to an explicit org.slf4j.Logger since lombok is not on the runtime classpath) inside the container against /app/jib-classpath-file; backed up the shipped AppLaunchController.class (md5 8f3639f387dc0437f4dee879f7f23623) and AppLaunchController$ProgressEvent.class (md5 c75f32fe6f90e8cb671fde3bb39052fc), swapped the pre-fix classes into /app/classes and restarted with case-launcher.enabled=true still set. POST /api/app-launch {patient-3, CL83303} returned 500 with message "need to implement this", and the container log recorded: Servlet.service() for servlet [dispatcherServlet] ... threw exception [Request processing failed: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException: need to implement this]. Restored both classes, md5s matched the backups exactly, restarted, and POST /api/app-launch {patient-0, CL83304} returned 200 again with the flag still true. (2) Metric flip: took the built SHA's own OperationService and TracingService sources and un-applied only this commit's hunk (2-arg getCaseLaunchCounter(mode, false) plus the case_launcher tag), compiled them and dropped them into /app/classes (which shadows the orci-utils jar), restarted, launched {patient-1, CL83305}: orci.case.launch came back as availableTags [{mode: INTERACTIVE},{case_launcher: ["false"]}] - the tag this ticket removes, seen red. Restored OperationService.class (md5 f02fa22e650521536e5cb217f60c1bf4, matches backup), deleted the TracingService shadow classes and /application.properties, restarted, and re-ran the positive: {patient-2, CL83306} returned 200, orci.case.launch showed only the mode tag, and /actuator/env contained no case-launcher key.

caveats: The two build-level deliverables (case-launcher module and its root-pom profile) have no runtime surface; they were confirmed only by their absence from the worktree, the pom, and the container's /app/libs and /actuator/beans.

The removed AppLaunchController branch was validated on the demo-demo tenant via the sheet-backed patient-N launch path; MGB and Mayo launch paths were not exercised, though the deleted branch was tenant-agnostic.

The orci.case.launch counter only increments on the operation-is-null branch of startOperation, so all launches used fresh case ids; the relaunch-existing-operation path does not touch the counter and was not part of the metric evidence.
The orphaned case-launcher ECR repository and the Spring Boot 2 cloudwatch property path noted in the ticket are explicit follow-ups and were not touched.

automation.assessment: qa-suite already has LAUNCH-001 in smoke/app-launch.spec.ts, which drives the clinical UI through /app-launch end to end - that is the regression this deletion could plausibly cause, and it is already covered on every run. There are no unit tests referencing AppLaunchController, getCaseLaunchCounter, or orci.case.launch, but the deleted code was unreachable-by-default dead code and the surviving metric call site is a single line with a constant argument removed; a test asserting a Micrometer tag set through the actuator would lock in plumbing, not behavior. Nothing new is worth adding.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A demo case launched end to end on the shipped build returned a full launch context, and orci.case.launch registered with only the mode tag.
Negative: Reinstating case-launcher.enabled=true on the running app changed nothing - launch still returned 200 and no case_launcher tag appeared.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix AppLaunchController back in made the same launch fail with UnsupportedOperationException, and un-applying the metric hunk brought the case_launcher tag back; both were reverted and the positive re-ran clean.

Automation: Existing smoke coverage of app launch is sufficient, so no new tests are proposed.
